topic: Local MCP server for web search + page fetch in Claude Code
projectName: Your planned local web-access MCP server (unbuilt)

recommendation.reason: Multiple official, mature, locally-runnable stdio MCP servers already expose exactly the must-have capability (web search + web page fetch) to Claude Code with the user's own or a free-tier API key. Tavily MCP, Brave Search MCP, and several no-key servers cover the full need; the user's real driver (control, own key, predictable behavior) is satisfied without new code, and Claude Code also ships built-in web tools. Building from scratch adds no capability these servers and the built-in tools do not already provide.
recommendation.reusableOption: Tavily MCP (tavily-ai/tavily-mcp) — official, Claude Code-native `claude mcp add` instructions, free 1000-credit/month tier, own key, broadest toolset (search/extract/map/crawl). If zero-cost/no-key is preferred, use @zhafron/mcp-web-search instead.
recommendation.biggestUnknown: Whether the user wants zero-cost/no-API-key search (scraping-based: @zhafron/mcp-web-search or nickclyde/duckduckgo-mcp-server, variable quality/rate-limits) versus a higher-quality API-backed search with a free tier (Tavily or Brave, requires registering a key). This preference was explicitly left open.

competitors.name: Tavily MCP
competitors.overview: Official Tavily MCP server (TypeScript/npm) exposing search, extract, map, and crawl tools; runs as a local stdio server or a hosted remote, with explicit Claude Code setup instructions and a free tier.

comparison.candidate: Local stdio (or hosted remote at mcp.tavily.com); Claude Code `claude mcp add` documented
Native: search, extract (page content), map, crawl
Own TAVILY_API_KEY; free Researcher plan 1000 credits/month, no credit card

notableDesigns.title: Search + extract + map + crawl in one server
notableDesigns.detail: Covers both must-have capabilities (search and page read) plus site mapping/crawling without a second server.

notableDesigns.title: Claude Code-native setup
notableDesigns.detail: README gives the exact `claude mcp add` command, so adoption is one command.

reusableLessons: Use a single API key env var (TAVILY_API_KEY) and expose focused tools (search/extract/map/crawl) rather than a generic fetch.
Offer a hosted remote transport alongside stdio so users can skip local install if they prefer.
competitors.summary: An official, Claude Code-native server that already delivers search + page read with a free tier and the user's own key — the unbuilt project's exact target, with no code to write.
competitors.coverageNote: Verified from official README and tavily.com/pricing (2026-08-29).

competitors.name: Brave Search MCP
competitors.overview: Official Brave Search MCP server (TypeScript/npm, @brave/brave-search-mcp-server) exposing web, local, video, image, and news search over the Brave Search API; stdio by default, own API key.

comparison.candidate: Own BRAVE_API_KEY; no separate free tier, each paid plan includes $5/month credit (~1000 searches)

notableDesigns.title: Typed search verticals
notableDesigns.detail: Separate tools for web/local/video/image/news search let the agent request a precise result type.

reusableLessons: Split search verticals into distinct tools so the agent can request the right result type.
Pair with the official Fetch server to add the page reading Brave lacks.
competitors.summary: Covers web search with an own-key, free-ish tier but not page reading — it would need a companion fetch server to match the full need.

competitors.name: @zhafron/mcp-web-search
competitors.overview: Community Node stdio MCP server providing multi-provider web search (DuckDuckGo/Bing/SearXNG with automatic fallback) and URL content extraction, with no API key required and built-in SSRF protection.

comparison.candidate: Node 18+ stdio; Claude Code config provided

notableDesigns.title: Multi-provider fallback with no key
notableDesigns.detail: Automatically falls back across DuckDuckGo/Bing/SearXNG, removing the API-key requirement entirely.

notableDesigns.title: SSRF protection on fetch_url
notableDesigns.detail: Guards the local server against server-side request forgery when fetching agent-supplied URLs.

reusableLessons: Ship a keyless default by scraping free engines with automatic provider fallback.
Always include SSRF protection on any fetch tool that follows agent-supplied URLs.
competitors.summary: The strongest zero-cost, zero-key option — both must-have capabilities with no registration — at the cost of scraping-based reliability.
competitors.coverageNote: Verified from official README (2026-08-29); scraping-based providers may rate-limit or break.

competitors.name: duckduckgo-mcp-server
competitors.overview: Community Python stdio MCP server (uvx) providing DuckDuckGo web search plus content fetching and parsing, with built-in rate limiting and no API key.

comparison.candidate: Python stdio via uvx; Claude Desktop config provided

notableDesigns.title: Built-in rate limiting
notableDesigns.detail: Throttles DuckDuckGo requests to avoid blocks without an API key.

reusableLessons: Add rate limiting when scraping a free engine to stay within its unwritten limits.
competitors.summary: A minimal no-key Python alternative covering both capabilities — simpler than @zhafron but single-engine.

competitors.name: Fetch (reference MCP server)
competitors.category: Ready-to-use official reference server (page fetch only)
competitors.overview: Official MCP reference Fetch server (Python, mcp-server-fetch) providing a fetch tool that retrieves a URL and converts HTML to markdown; stdio, no API key. Covers page reading only, not search.

comparison.candidate: Python stdio via uvx; no key
Native page fetch only; no web search

notableDesigns.title: HTML to markdown with pagination
notableDesigns.detail: fetch(url, max_length, start_index) returns clean markdown and supports paging long pages to fit context windows.

reusableLessons: Convert fetched HTML to markdown and paginate long content to fit agent context windows.
This server can reach local/internal IPs — restrict that for untrusted input.
competitors.summary: The official baseline for the page-read half of the need; pair it with a search server if you split the two capabilities.

unknowns: Whether the user prefers zero-cost/no-key scraping search (lower, variable quality) vs. an API-backed search with a free tier (higher quality, requires registering a key).
Whether Claude Code's built-in web tools already meet the user's day-to-day needs, making even an MCP server optional.
Long-term reliability and rate-limits of scraping-based no-key servers (DuckDuckGo/Bing) under regular agent use.
